stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about long-term skin-cancer risk, which patient characteristic aligns with standard references?

options.text: Fitzpatrick skin types I to III
Fitzpatrick skin types V to VI only
Skin type never influences post-transplant skin-cancer risk
Only recipients younger than 18 years are at increased skin-cancer risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors in transplant recipients include skin type (Fitzpatrick I to III), cumulative sun exposure, older age at transplant, immunosuppression intensity, and transplant type.

rationale_incorrect.B: Lighter Fitzpatrick skin types I to III are specifically listed rather than types V to VI alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Skin type is among cited risk factors rather than having no influence.
rationale_incorrect.D: Risk factors apply across adult recipients rather than being limited to recipients younger than 18 years.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → skin cancer → Risk factors → i.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → skin cancer → Risk factors → i. (Fitzpatrick skin types I–III); PDF p. 280 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fitzpatrick skin-type risk angle distinct from heart/lung incidence counseling (cctc-2108) and 95% BCC/SCC epidemiology (cctc-2105); anchor verified on Cupples p. 280.

stem: During pretransplant malignancy-prevention teaching, which sun-precaution principle aligns with standard references?

options.text: Maximize midday sun exposure to improve vitamin D without precautions
Sun avoidance is unnecessary after transplantation
Only kidney recipients need sun precautions

explanation.rationale_correct: Cancer-prevention teaching includes sun precautions such as avoiding undue exposure to sunlight, avoiding tanning beds, wearing protective clothing, and using sunscreen with minimum SPF 50.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sun precautions are recommended rather than maximizing unprotected midday exposure.
rationale_incorrect.C: Sun precautions remain important after transplantation because immunosuppression increases skin-cancer risk.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sun precautions apply to transplant recipients broadly rather than kidney recipients alone.

references.locator: Ch. 6 → Prevention of cancer → 4.a. (avoid undue sunlight exposure); PDF p. 282 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Undue-sunlight avoidance angle distinct from tanning-bed item (cctc-1102) and ACS screening minimum (cctc-2151); anchor verified on Cupples p. 282.

stem: A liver transplant candidate asks what sunscreen characteristics align with standard malignancy-prevention references. Which counseling point is correct?

options.text: Use sunscreen that provides ultraviolet-B protection with minimum SPF 50
Any sunscreen with SPF 15 is sufficient regardless of transplant status
Sunscreen is never recommended for transplant candidates or recipients
Only tanning-bed lotions provide adequate post-transplant sun protection

explanation.rationale_correct: Sun precautions include using sunscreen lotion that provides protection against ultraviolet-B rays with a minimum sun protection factor of 50, along with protective clothing and avoiding tanning beds.

rationale_incorrect.B: Minimum SPF 50 ultraviolet-B protection is specified rather than SPF 15 alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Sunscreen is recommended as part of cancer-prevention teaching.
rationale_incorrect.D: Tanning beds should be avoided rather than using tanning-bed lotions for protection.

stem: A coordinator is updating skin-cancer prevention teaching for the evaluation team. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Fitzpatrick skin types I to III are cited skin-cancer risk factors.
Recipients should avoid undue exposure to sunlight.
Tanning beds are a safe alternative to sun avoidance.
Sunscreen should provide ultraviolet-B protection with minimum SPF 50.

explanation.rationale_correct: Fitzpatrick skin types I to III, avoiding undue sunlight, and minimum SPF 50 ultraviolet-B sunscreen are supported. Statement III is false because tanning beds should be avoided rather than used as a safe alternative.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—minimum SPF 50 ultraviolet-B sunscreen is recommended.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because tanning beds are specifically avoided.
